payout_quote: Deposit is 5 cents per container except for liquor which has a deposit of 15 cents per container
steps: Buy covered beverages in Vermont (5¢ deposit; 15¢ on liquor containers over 50ml)
Keep empties — clean and unbroken, with the VT redemption message
Return to a retailer (must take back brands they sell) or a certified redemption center (must accept all covered containers)
catches: This returns YOUR OWN deposit money paid at purchase — it is recovering your own money, not new income.
Only containers bought in-state with the correct deposit label are redeemable; out-of-state containers are ineligible and redeeming them is fraud.
Wine and hard cider are NOT covered in Vermont; liquor-bottle deposits fund the Liquor Control Enterprise Fund if unclaimed.
biggest_catch: Returns your own deposit — you paid it at purchase. This is deposit recovery, not income.
eligibility: Anyone returning covered containers purchased in Vermont.
timing: Refund paid at return (retailers/certified centers must redeem ≥40 hrs/week).

c1.evidence: Vermont Agency of Natural Resources / legislature.vermont.gov Bottle Bill overview (10 V.S.A. Chapter 53).

c3.evidence: No fee; deposit already paid at purchase.

c4.evidence: 5¢/15¢ per container; statute 10 V.S.A. §1522 confirms refund to consumer on return.

s1.note: Covered containers purchased in Vermont (beer, malt, carbonated drinks, liquor).

s6.note: Steps are concrete: buy, save, return to retailer/center, get refund.

notes: Vermont passed the first US bottle bill (1973); wine and hard cider remain excluded.

numeric_basis: payout from official VT terms (5¢/15¢ per container); time: collecting empties + return trip est. 20–60 min active.
